title: Segmented bucket smoothing for reserved pool rollovers and burst absorption
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Customers on Reserved capacity experience two classes of issues around limit resets and short bursts: 1) rigid monthly/daily reset boundaries cause sudden availability cliffs for bursty tenants (applications that have daily peaks), and 2) our existing hard-reset model forces immediate quota truncation which either drops requests or causes fallbacks to shared capacity with no predictable smoothing. This ticket proposes a 'segmented bucket smoothing' approach: split each tenant's quota window into a small set of overlapping micro-buckets (segments) that roll over in a staggered fashion. On reset, rather than all credit appearing or disappearing at once, credits are added/removed across segments to provide a graceful slope. Goals: reduce failed requests during boundary windows, preserve billing accuracy, and keep predictable latency/SLOs for Dedicated pools.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by infra and billing leads
Migration strategy for ledger and usage cache that is idempotent and can be backfilled
Smoothing algorithm implemented in quota service with feature flag
End-to-end tests covering edge cases (timezone shifts, tenant timezone changes, DST transitions)
Performance benchmark: no >5% p95 latency regression for quota checks under 10k rps in dedicated pool
Cost/accuracy: less than 0.1% divergence vs consolidated monthly counters after 30 days of backfill
implementation_notes: Architecture: introduce segment metadata (N segments per tenant, segment_size_seconds) stored in quota-config table. Quota check will consult active segments (sliding window) and compute available tokens = sum(remaining in active segments). On allocation, tokens consumed from oldest non-empty segment. On reset/rollover scheduler, credits are applied to segments in a staggered fashion. Reconciler: nightly background job reconciles cross-check between fast in-memory KV cache and canonical ledger to correct drift. Migration: incremental backfill job that converts existing single-window entries into segment view using historical usage fingerprint. DB changes minimal: add columns segment_count, segment_epoch_base, last_reconciled_at. Feature flag gating via flags-service.
tradeoffs_and_alternatives: Option A (chosen): Segmented smoothing provides graceful transitions and keeps per-tenant accounting accurate, but increases complexity in quota-check hot path and requires careful cache invalidation.
Option B: Soft-limits with probabilistic admission (throttle with sampling) — simpler but yields non-deterministic billing and worse developer experience for enterprise tenants.
Option C: Keep hard resets and push client-side advisories — lowest infra risk but unacceptable customer impact for Dedicated customers.
Decision: implement Option A behind FF; monitor overhead; revert to hard-reset behavior if >8% p95 latency regression observed in canary region.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Deploy segment schema + FF without changing runtime behavior. Phase 2: Run backfill simulator on staging using 30 days of real traffic snapshots to tune segment_count (default 6) and segment_size. Phase 3: Enable smoothing for 10% of tenants in canary (low-impact customers), monitor fail rates and billing convergence. Phase 4: Gradual ramp to all Dedicated tenants with weekly reconciler enabled. Provide 'revert to hard-reset' quick flag and rollback playbook.
monitoring_and_signals: Grafana dashboards: ReservedQuota.Smoothing.AvailableTokens, ReservedQuota.Smoothing.CheckLatency, ReservedQuota.Reconciler.DriftErrors. Alerts: increase in rejections at window boundaries (>25% baseline) OR reconciler error rate >0.5% for 1h. Add billing QA job to compare ledger totals vs aggregated segments daily.
performance_estimates: Expected: median quota-check cost +5% CPU for quota-service, p95 latency change <5% in benchmarks. Operational win: 30-60% reduction in boundary-time request failures for bursty tenants in pilot (observed in staging sims).
